incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGERDUTY P1 triggered — multiple model load failures reported from eu-west-1-gpupool-3. Error pattern: OOM at model deserialization / compile timeout. Paging @alex (oncall), @maria (runtime). 

alex: grabbing this — can everyone paste recent logs if you have them?

maria: seeing repeated failures during model warmup. stack snippet below from one of the crashes:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 14.76 GiB total capacity; 12.11 GiB already allocated; 1.12 GiB free; 12.31 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
File "serve/runtime/loader.py", line 214, in load_model
  model = torch.jit.load(path)
```

devon: also seeing compile-time hangs in the kernel selection step: nvrtc shows repeated timeouts ~120s then container dies. Log: `NVRTC: compilation timeout after 120s`

jess: initial triage — appears correlated with a new model rollout 10:12 UTC (large 70B variant) plus a change to auto-quantize = true in the deployment config. Could be memory spike at load + JIT compile.

alex: immediate mitigation plan:
- stop loading the new 70B model on the affected pool
- evict model artifacts from nodes showing flaps
- failover traffic to fallback pool eu-west-1-fallback (smaller capacity but healthy)
- roll back auto-quantize flag for that deployment

maria: executing evict on node gpu-12 now. Command I ran:
```
# evict model from node
redwoodctl node evict --node gpu-12 --model-id mdl-70B-2026-03-15
```
restarting container for gpu-12 (restart command issued).

devon: starting a warmup on fallback with a 4-bit quantized variant as a safety. If that warms successfully we can resume traffic there.

sre-oncall: switched routing to fallback pool with this API call:
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.redwood.internal/v1/routing/switch \
  -d '{"from":"eu-west-1-gpupool-3","to":"eu-west-1-fallback","models":["mdl-70B-2026-03-15"]}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
(rolled at 10:24 UTC)

customer-success: ping — we have inbound reports of errors from 3 enterprise customers (request 503s). Estimated impact start 10:12 UTC.

alex: status update 10:30 UTC — evictions succeeded on 2/3 bad nodes, one node (gpu-14) repeatedly reboots. Node appears to have GPU driver crashing and causing docker OOM. Opening infra ticket.

anil: I see kernel driver OOM logs on gpu-14:
```
[drm:amdgpu_ttm_bo_evict] *ERROR* failed to evict BO, mmap count leaked
Dec  3 10:29:17 gpu-14 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31: Fatal MMU fault
```
container runtime shows exit code 137 shortly after.

jess: mitigation — I've disabled auto-compile for the rollout so JIT doesn't trigger long NVRTC runs. Command:
```
redwoodctl deployment update --id rollout-587 --set "runtime.auto_compile=false"
```
That should prevent new compile attempts while we stabilize.

maria: warmup of 4-bit variant on fallback completed at 10:38 UTC, passes health checks. Routing fully active to fallback at 10:40 UTC.

alex: handoff — I'll be on-call for next 30 minutes to monitor and then hand to @jess for long-term follow-up. Current severity: P1 -> Customer impact reduced due to failover but still classified as P1 until nodes stable.

sre-oncall: summary of immediate impact: ~18 minutes of elevated 5xx for some customers, majority traffic now healthy on fallback. No user data access issues.

customer-success: notified affected customers at 10:45 UTC. Template message posted to accounts: "We experienced transient 5xx errors affecting model loads between 10:12–10:30 UTC; traffic has been rerouted and we’ll follow up with RCA."

anil: infra action items: cordon gpu-14, run driver forensic, consider kernel/gpu firmware rollback if driver crash reproducible.

devon: we should add a guard in runtime to reject model loads that exceed per-node pre-reserved memory threshold and fall back before OOM. Filing an engineering issue: https://issues.redwood.internal/RED-3321

alex: taking meeting with infra in 15 to decide node action. I'll update thread after handoff. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident recorded — ticket INC-2026-1795 created, linked to PD alert.

jess: (handoff) taking long-term. Next steps for postmortem:
- RCA: distinguish driver vs workload (compilation spike vs deserialization memory use)
- Add pre-load memory checks and better fallback for large models
- Add compile-time timeout/backoff and fallback-to-precompiled artifact
- Improve customer-facing incident timeline and metrics

alex: last status 10:55 UTC — fallback stable, nodes drained where possible. handing to jess.

jess: closing the active paging loop in 10 min — will keep monitoring and will file RCA within 48 hours. If anyone has logs/metrics not in the ticket, please attach.

anil: note — we observed one node with persistent kernel Xid 31 after repeated restarts, possible hardware fault. Will schedule replacement if driver rollback doesn't help.

customer-success: all customers acknowledged the initial notice, one asked for exact affected models (sent list).

alex: thank you team — good quick response. :raised_hands:
